verdict.rationale: Reflect's docs say note contents are end-to-end encrypted so 'no one else can read them (not even us),' which means its servers cannot read note contents to train on them. Users can also mark notes private to exclude them from AI features, and can bring their own API key so requests go directly to their chosen provider. However, the evidence contains no explicit no-training policy or training opt-out, so prevention is only implied by the architecture. Missing for 10: an explicit statement that user data is never used for model training, documented guarantees about training use by the OpenAI/Anthropic models used for AI features, coverage of uploaded files (which the E2E encryption reportedly does not cover), and independent corroboration.
